key_insight: A hybrid MILP–QUBO framework delivers verified routing improvements with SQBM+, while QAOA tests identify a current hardware boundary of 4 customers (16 qubits) for reliable constraint satisfaction.
engineering_relevance: Vehicle-level decomposition offers a practical way to test quantum optimization within routing workflows while validating feasibility and accepting only improvements over classical baselines.
method: Combine classical MILP with vehicle-level QUBO route optimization.
Solve subproblems using Toshiba SQBM+ and QAOA on Rigetti Ankaa-3 and IQM Emerald processors.
Validate operational constraints and require monotone improvement over classical baselines.
evidence_signal: Across five London-derived benchmarks with 10–70 customers, SQBM+ reduced verified fleet distance by 2.80% (7,927 m) for 25 customers and 0.22% (1,186 m) for 55 customers.
watch_item: Assignment-level time-window tightness remains the dominant scalability bottleneck, and these results do not establish quantum advantage.
paper_title: Hybrid Classical-Quantum Optimization for CVRPTW: A Systems Framework with Provable Feasibility and Empirical Hardware Limits
